articles.title: Bonta on Nvidia: "Companies cannot mislead their investors"

facts.fact: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has served Nvidia with an investigative subpoena.

His office wants to know whether the company's advanced chips or confidential information may have gone to China. It is also asking whether Nvidia misled investors and the public, the California Department of Justice said in a statement on Thursday.
"Companies cannot mislead their investors," Bonta said.
The department said the subpoena relates to former chief executive Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Huang resigned as chief executive last week after revelations of extramarital affairs, Reuters reported.
US intelligence agencies are trying to establish her ties to China's Ministry of State Security, according to Reuters. China rejects the espionage allegations.
Nvidia's board has ruled out his return and set up a national security committee. Huang has agreed to appear before House committees on 1 December.

Also on Thursday, the House Foreign Affairs Committee said the Trump administration had approved nearly 900,000 advanced Nvidia and AMD AI chips for Chinese companies, Reuters reported. The approvals ran from December 2025 to May.
Nvidia told Reuters the approvals had strict conditions and limited volumes. It said it had stopped shipping H200 chips to China.

stories.title: OpenAI adds up to 40% API discount if developers let GPT-6.2 jobs finish in 2 or 8 hours
stories.note: Read via AI Times (Korea), which embeds OpenAI Developers' 11-18 post. Event is 11-18, outlet article is today. Facts are English renderings of Korean text. OpenAI primary page not read.

articles.title: 오픈AI, 'GPT-6.2' 응답 늦게 받으면 API 요금 최대 40% 할인

facts.fact: OpenAI introduced a new billing option that varies API prices by response time.
Setting the target completion time of an API request to 2 hours or 8 hours earns a discount: 30% cheaper than standard for 2 hours, 40% cheaper for 8 hours.
The option is a 'Completion Window' added to the background mode of the Responses API.
It applies to four models, GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6.2 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra and GPT-6 Luna, and is in public beta.
The discount also applies to multi-step agent tasks, if follow-up requests meet the discount conditions.
OpenAI's own post: "For single- or multi-turn workflows that can wait, save up to 40% per token than Standard on GPT-6.2 Astra or GPT-6.2 Sol."
The change is linked to OpenAI replacing 'Flex' processing with a time-based discount option; Flex is not offered on GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol.

articles.title: 문샷 AI, 미국 수출 규제에 2000억 규모 엔비디아 칩 임대 계약 취소

facts.fact: Moonshot AI cancelled a $150 million (about 200 billion won) deal to rent Nvidia's latest AI chips through an Indonesian data center.
The Information reported on the 19th (US time), citing multiple sources, that Moonshot withdrew from the Blackwell Ultra B300 rental deal with a Southeast Asian neocloud company.
Moonshot had reportedly accepted paying 50% of the contract up front; the usual prepayment ratio is about 15%.
The trigger is a new US Commerce Department rule announced on the 16th and in force from the 19th.
The rule requires overseas data centers serving Chinese customers above a certain size to get US government permission.
Data centers already serving Chinese firms above that size must get a US licence within 90 days; the threshold is compute equal to about 300 of the latest AI chips.
Moonshot has also paused negotiations on other new GPU rental deals while it reviews the rule's impact.
Moonshot's K3 model, released in July, drew attention for performance comparable to major US models; it was seeking more GPUs for its next model, Kimi K4.

stories.title: Google picks Blue Origin's New Glenn to launch its AI-chip satellites for Project Suncatcher in 2029

articles.title: 구글, 우주 AI 데이터센터 구축 위해 블루 오리진과 계약...2029년 위성 발사

facts.fact: Google chose Jeff Bezos' space company Blue Origin as launch partner for its Project Suncatcher experiment to build solar-powered AI data centers in space.
Blue Origin said on the 19th (US time) that Google selected its large New Glenn rocket and signed a launch services contract.
The first dedicated launch is planned for the first quarter of 2029, carrying several compute satellites with Google's TPU chips.
Each satellite will have compute power equal to one standard data center server rack.
The satellites would sit in a sun-synchronous orbit with near-constant sunlight.
Google launched a first test satellite built with Planet Labs on a SpaceX Falcon 9 in October; it is operating normally.
Next year Google plans an experiment linking two satellites; the first test satellite already ran the Gemma 4 model.
SpaceX and startup Starcloud are also pursuing space data centers; launch cost, satellite output, radiation shielding and cooling remain open challenges.

stories.title: Google built a fake internet, 'Mirror Dimension', to test AI agents against prompt-injection attacks
stories.note: heise only (German, cites Wired). Morning post was heise; avoid heise-only lead. Google's own post not read.

articles.title: Google baut ein künstliches Internet für seine KI-Agenten

facts.fact: Google has created an artificial internet with thousands of websites to expose AI agents to realistic attacks and improve their security.
The 'Mirror Dimension' is a test environment sealed off from the real internet, with thousands of artificial websites.
Prompt-injection attacks hide instructions on websites to divert agents from their real task, for example to leak confidential user data.
AI models sometimes notice they are being tested and change behaviour, so the fake sites must look real.
Agents visit real addresses such as youtube.com; Chrome runs in an isolated environment that redirects all traffic to a local proxy serving artificial versions.
AI agents build the websites: a research agent finds requirements, a development agent codes the sites, other agents review them.
According to Google, the automated test pipeline generates more than 1,000 attack test candidates per security engineer per day, over 30 times as many as manual work.
According to Wired, the test environment is to be opened to other teams in the company.

stories.title: OpenAI's Codex-based 'Performance Factory' investigated 1,700 ChatGPT performance issues but shipped only 15 unedited fixes
stories.note: Morning dropped OpenAI page (403); readable now via AI Times. English renderings of Korean text.

articles.title: 오픈AI, 코덱스로 챗GPT 성능 문제 자동 진단·수정안 작성

facts.fact: OpenAI revealed an internal automated system built on Codex that finds causes of ChatGPT performance drops and helps fix them.
OpenAI described the system, 'Performance Factory', on the 19th (US time).
In about three months it investigated more than 1,700 performance issues and found root causes for more than 600, about 17 automatic investigations per day.
About 400 of the diagnosed cases reached the fix-proposal stage, but only 15 deployed fixes used Codex-written code as written.
Multiple agents split roles: one finds the cause, another verifies, and Codex writes the fix and submits it to GitHub.
Engineers review and deploy the fix; the system then checks whether performance recovered.
One agent blamed an image download error for failed conversations; a reviewing agent found the related service had already recovered and had the investigation redone.
Code changes and deployment are still approved by engineers.

articles.title: Meta's new Muse Charm device may cost $300

facts.fact: Meta plans to charge $300 for Muse Charm, its upcoming Tamagotchi-like AI device that was teased at the company's Connect event earlier this year, The Information has reported.

When reached for comment by TechCrunch, a Meta spokesperson didn't deny the claims, merely providing the following statement: "We're charmed by the interest in our AI devices, and we'll have more to share soon."

Muse Charm will allow users to carry a physical personification of its software around in their pocket (or potentially wear it around their neck), talking to it, asking it questions, and giving it commands.
The wearable launched by Friend, the AI startup whose device lets you text and talk to an AI persona, is currently retailing for $250.
Amazon's all-new Bee Frontier wearable AI device lists for $75 and is currently on a Black Friday, 30% off sale of $52.49.
Even with its $99/year subscription to let it tie into a user's apps (photos, emails, etc.), it's still far less expensive than Muse Charm.
Meta has made a relatively successful push into consumer AI, launching Muse, its agentic helper, along with a variety of cute avatars.

stories.note: Source is Bloomberg via TechCrunch; Apple did not respond. Early stage.

articles.title: Apple may be developing its own AI agent that runs your Mac

facts.fact: Apple appears to be working on its own AI agent to conduct computer work on behalf of users, including using apps, accessing websites, and coding.

The news was originally reported by Bloomberg, which spotted a job listing the iPhone maker recently posted for a senior engineering manager to oversee the creation of an "AI agent that can use a computer."
"Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does," the posting says.
The agents should be able to move "fluidly between tools" and "carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs."
Bloomberg notes that the version of its upcoming macOS 27.3 will deploy warnings discouraging users from granting full access to third-party agents.
Bloomberg says the iPhone maker "has eyed introducing the service as soon as the end of next year," but progress "remains in the early stages."
TechCrunch reached out to Apple for more information but did not receive a response.

articles.title: Google's Gemini can now take over tasks on your Mac

facts.fact: Google is rolling out computer use in its Gemini app for Mac, letting the assistant carry out multi-step tasks across local files, desktop apps and websites in a separate background window.
It runs in a separate background window with a live preview in the chat, so your screen and cursor stay free.
You choose which apps it can use, can pause it, and must approve key actions.
The feature is for paying subscribers to Google's AI Plus, Pro and Ultra plans, and needs a Mac with Apple Silicon.
As with its Gemini Spark agent, it is not available in Europe or the UK.
Google warns that Gemini can make mistakes, including permanently deleting files or sharing them with others.
Backups of changed files are deleted after 24 hours or when you start a new task.

articles.title: Anthropic's 7 founders cashed out nearly $2B in record-breaking IPO

facts.fact: Anthropic became a public company on Thursday, raising a total of $81.3 billion, including $1.95 billion for its seven founders.
At the upgraded IPO price of $83 per share, each founder pocketed about $280 million before underwriting fees and taxes.
Each of the founders has pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal equity in the company to philanthropy.
The company points out that these commitments are "voluntary, revocable expressions of each co-founder's philanthropic intent and do not constitute legally binding obligations."
Nvidia bought $10 billion of the special non-voting Class N shares, Google bought $10 billion, and AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC divvied up the rest.
Google wound up owning 13.4% of the company; Amazon has 14.6%; together 28%.
Anthropic needs about $70.7 billion just to cover its compute and infrastructure spending commitments in the next 12 months, and $451.6 billion before the end of 2030.
When Facebook had its record-breaking IPO in 2012, it raised $16 billion on IPO day.
